key_insight: Burst restarts in wall turbulence can be explained by a forced linearised channel-flow model, where vortex breakup and catch-up dynamics set a linearly available energy threshold for re-ignition.
engineering_relevance: The result provides a reduced-order framework for predicting and controlling near-wall burst regeneration in turbulence models and wall-bounded flow design.
method: Formulate a forced linearised Navier–Stokes system for a log-minimal channel, with forcing representing nonlinear interactions.
Solve optimisation problems to identify minimal conditions that enable burst-restart-like solutions.
Define linearly available energy (LAE) to track the restart process and compare linear-model and real-turbulence flow patterns.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports qualitative comparison of optimised linearised solutions and flow patterns extracted from real turbulence during the restart stage, showing consistent breakup and merging behavior.
watch_item: The framework is model- and flow-regime-specific, so LAE thresholds and restart mechanisms may not transfer directly outside the log-minimal channel setting.
paper_title: Restarts of bursts in turbulence in a log-minimal channel
